sections.name: The $15 Boards
sections.intro: Small gatherings, a wine night, a movie night, dessert. Two cheeses, one meat, one cracker and one fruit is enough to make a board feel like a board, and these four prove it.

sections.name: The $30 Boards
sections.intro: The everyday party board. At $30 for ten you can't buy fancy cheese, but you can buy plenty, and smart arrangement makes plenty look generous.

sections.name: The $50 Boards
sections.intro: The step up most hosts notice. Fifty dollars buys a second cured meat, a cheese with real character, or a theme built on real ingredients.

sections.name: The $100 Boards
sections.intro: Cheese-counter territory. A hundred dollars buys aged and imported cheeses, French deli foods, or a full pound of smoked salmon and two pounds of shrimp.

sections.name: The $250 Boards
sections.intro: The splurge. Caviar, long-aged Parmigiano and Prosciutto di Parma, prize-winning American cheese, acorn-fed jamón and fresh truffle: the foods people remember.

sections.name: The Crowd Boards
sections.sub: For 20 to 100 guests · about $3 a guest
sections.intro: Graduations, showers, office parties and reunions. These boards sit beside other food, so they plan a little less per person and lean on cheap, popular foods bought in bulk.

boards.title: Snack Board for Four
boards.label: $15 for 4
boards.buys: Fifteen dollars buys two cheeses, one salami and the two things every board needs: a cracker and a fruit. Nothing here is fancy, but a soft cheese next to a sharp one is the oldest pairing trick there is.
boards.drink: Pinot Grigio, cider or sparkling water

timeline.what: Take the brie out of the fridge so it softens.
Slice the cheddar and cut the brie into 8 wedges.
Fold the salami into quarters.
Rinse and dry the grapes; snip into small clusters.
Build the board and fill the gaps with crackers.

boards.title: Movie Night Snack Board
boards.label: $15 for 4
boards.buys: A movie board is about grazing for two hours, so fifteen dollars goes to salty, crunchy foods that last: popcorn, pretzels and cheese cubes, with chocolate for the sweet tooth.
boards.drink: Root beer, lager or sparkling water

timeline.what: Cut both cheeses into bite-size cubes.
Pop one bag of popcorn and let it cool for 5 minutes.
Snip the grapes into small clusters.
Break the chocolate into squares.
Build the board and press play.

boards.title: Wine Night for Four
boards.label: $15 for 4
boards.buys: Fifteen dollars covers one good soft cheese and a little prosciutto, the two things that taste most expensive. Fig spread and dried fruit do the rest of the work for very little money.
boards.drink: Pinot Noir, Rosé or a dry Riesling

timeline.what: Take the brie out to soften.
Cut the brie into 6 slim slices.
Separate the prosciutto slices so they don't tear.
Spoon the fig spread into a ramekin.
Pour the wine and build the board.

boards.title: Sweet and Salty Dessert Board
boards.label: $15 for 4
boards.buys: A dessert board costs less than a cheese board because chocolate and cookies are cheap per bite. Fifteen dollars buys a dip, fresh fruit, two chocolates, two crunchy things and a bag of marshmallows.
boards.drink: Coffee, port or cold milk

timeline.what: Wash and dry the strawberries; halve a few.
Spoon the spread into a ramekin.
Break both chocolate bars into squares.
Open the pretzels, wafers and marshmallows.
Build the board.

boards.title: The Classic for Ten
boards.label: $30 for 10
boards.buys: This is the Charcuterie Lab Price Index basket turned into a board: the classic board for ten at about $3 a guest. Moving up from $15 buys party amounts, enough salami for a river, and olives, almonds and fig spread for two small dishes.
boards.drink: Pinot Noir, Chardonnay or a pale ale

timeline.what: Take out the brie. Slice both cheddar blocks.
Cut the brie into 8 wedges.
Fold the salami; drain the olives.
Fill the ramekins. Snip the grapes.
Build the board.

boards.title: Game Day Board
boards.label: $30 for 10
boards.buys: Game day food has to survive four quarters, so $30 goes to sturdy, salty foods: two sausages, two cheeses, pretzels and pickles, with mustard and ranch for dipping.
boards.drink: Lager, amber ale or cola

timeline.what: Slice one summer sausage into thick coins; keep the second for halftime.
Cube the cheddar and pepper jack.
Drain the pickles; fill the mustard and ranch ramekins.
Open the pretzels, crackers and carrots.
Build the board before kickoff.

boards.title: Mediterranean Mezze Board
boards.label: $30 for 10
boards.buys: Dips and vegetables cost far less than cured meat, so $30 buys a big, colorful board with no meat at all: two dips, feta, dolmas, two olives and fresh vegetables.
boards.drink: Sauvignon Blanc, dry rosé or mint lemonade

timeline.what: Cut the feta into cubes; drizzle with oil and oregano.
Slice the cucumbers; halve some tomatoes.
Spoon the dips into bowls; add oil and paprika to the hummus.
Cut the pita into triangles; drain the dolmas and olives.
Build the board.

boards.title: Brunch Board
boards.label: $30 for 10
boards.buys: Brunch is cheaper than cheese hour: bagels, eggs and fruit are filling and inexpensive. $30 buys a full brunch spread for ten with ham, Swiss and two fruits.
boards.drink: Orange juice, coffee or mimosas

timeline.what: Hard-boil 5 eggs (12 minutes), then chill in ice water.
Halve and toast the bagels.
Peel and halve the eggs; pepper the yolks.
Fold the ham and Swiss. Peel the clementines.
Build the board.

boards.title: Italian Antipasto Board
boards.label: $50 for 10
boards.buys: At $50 you get two cured meats instead of one and the jarred antipasto classics. A warehouse club's big jars cost less per ounce, and leftovers keep for weeks.
boards.drink: Chianti, Pinot Grigio or Italian soda

timeline.what: Slice and toast one baguette.
Drain the mozzarella pearls; toss with oil and pepper.
Drain the artichokes, peppers and olives into bowls.
Fold the salami, capicola and provolone.
Build the board.

boards.title: Cheese Lover's Board
boards.label: $50 for 10
boards.buys: Fifty dollars buys five different cheeses, each a different style: aged, soft, sharp, blue and fresh. No meat at all, which leaves room for nuts, fruit and two crackers.
boards.drink: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir or tawny port

timeline.what: Take out every cheese except the goat log.
Cut each cheese its own way (see step 1).
Slice the goat log into rounds; drizzle with honey.
Slice the apple; snip the grapes.
Build the board.

boards.title: Smokehouse BBQ Board
boards.label: $50 for 10
boards.buys: This is the meat-heavy rung: $50 buys two sausages seared hot, summer sausage, jerky and smoked cheese, with cornbread you bake from a cheap mix.
boards.drink: Amber ale, bourbon lemonade or sweet tea
pantry: 2 eggs and 2/3 cup milk for the cornbread

timeline.what: Bake the cornbread in an 8-inch pan (about 20 min).
Slice the smoked sausage on the bias and sear until browned.
Slice the summer sausage; cut the gouda and cheddar.
Cut the cornbread into squares; fill the sauce ramekins.
Build the board while the sausage is warm.

boards.title: Spanish Tapas Board
boards.label: $50 for 10
boards.buys: At $50 the board can be built around real Spanish foods: Manchego, dry-cured chorizo and quince paste. Tomato bread, a Spanish staple, costs almost nothing to make.
boards.drink: Tempranillo, dry sherry or sangria

timeline.what: Slice the Manchego into thin triangles.
Cut the quince paste into thin squares.
Slice and toast the baguette; rub with garlic and cut tomato.
Slice the chorizo; drain the olives and peppers.
Build the board.

boards.title: Wine and Cheese Tasting Board
boards.label: $100 for 10
boards.buys: One hundred dollars moves the board to the cheese counter: five cheeses chosen to taste from mild to strong, plus honeycomb, marcona almonds and fresh pears.
boards.drink: A white, a light red and a full red

timeline.what: Take out the Gruyère, gouda and gorgonzola.
Take out the brie and goat cheese.
Cut each cheese (see step 1); slice the baguette.
Slice the pears so they don't brown; snip the grapes.
Pour the first wine and build.

boards.title: French Bistro Board
boards.label: $100 for 10
boards.buys: At $100 you can buy French deli foods: country pâté, saucisson sec, a French brie and a wedge of Comté. Radishes with butter and salt are the classic Paris bistro snack.
boards.drink: Beaujolais, Côtes du Rhône or Champagne

timeline.what: Take out the brie and the butter.
Slice the pâté and saucisson.
Cut the Comté into triangles and the brie into slices.
Halve the radishes; slice the baguettes.
Build the board.

boards.title: Smoked Fish and Seafood Board
boards.label: $100 for 10
boards.buys: Seafood is where a warehouse club saves the most. $100 buys a pound of smoked salmon and two pounds of cooked shrimp, with all the classic toppings.
boards.drink: Dry Riesling, Champagne or a crisp lager

timeline.what: Thaw the shrimp overnight in the fridge.
Mix one block of cream cheese with chopped dill.
Finely dice half a red onion; rinse it in cold water.
Slice the cucumber; cut the lemons into wedges.
Fill a bowl with ice, add the shrimp and build.

boards.title: Salumi Lover's Board
boards.label: $100 for 10
boards.buys: At $100 the meat takes over: four Italian cured meats, each shown a different way, with Parmigiano chunks, provolone, giardiniera and focaccia.
boards.drink: Sangiovese, Barbera or an Italian pilsner

timeline.what: Break the Parmigiano into chunks with a short knife.
Wrap 6 breadsticks with prosciutto.
Fold the capicola, Genoa and provolone.
Cut the focaccia into squares; drain the giardiniera.
Build the board.

boards.title: Caviar and Champagne Board
boards.label: $250 for 10
boards.buys: Two hundred fifty dollars buys real caviar, the one luxury that changes a board completely. Everything else on the board is there to serve it: blini, crème fraîche, egg, chives and shallot.
boards.drink: Champagne or a dry sparkling wine

timeline.what: Hard-boil 5 eggs; chill, peel and halve.
Press the yolks through a sieve; chop the chives and shallot.
Cut the triple-crème into wedges; fold the salmon.
Warm the blini in a low oven with a little butter.
Set the caviar on ice last and open the tin at the table.

boards.title: Italian Salumeria Board
boards.label: $250 for 10
boards.buys: At $250 the board is built on Italy's protected classics: 30-month Parmigiano Reggiano, 24-month Prosciutto di Parma and a traditional aged balsamic poured a few drops at a time, with fresh burrata to tear open at the table.
boards.drink: Barolo, Brunello or Franciacorta

items.name: Traditional balsamic vinegar of Modena, aged

timeline.what: Take out the Parmigiano and gorgonzola.
Break the Parmigiano into craggy chunks.
Separate the prosciutto slices; fold the mortadella.
Halve the figs; drain the olives.
Tear the burrata at the table.

boards.title: Award-Winning American Cheese Board
boards.label: $250 for 10
boards.buys: This is where $250 goes furthest for cheese lovers: six American farmstead cheeses in six different styles, the kind that win national competitions, from a good cheese shop.
boards.drink: Dry cider, Pinot Noir or a Belgian-style ale

items.name: Champagne grapes or seedless red grapes

timeline.what: Take out all six cheeses.
Cut each cheese (see step 1).
Peel back the top rind on the spruce-bark round.
Slice the pears; set out the honeycomb.
Build the board.

boards.title: Truffle and Jamón Ibérico Board
boards.label: $250 for 10
boards.buys: Two of the most expensive foods on any board share this one: acorn-fed jamón ibérico and fresh black truffle. Each guest gets a real taste of both, which is the point of a splurge.
boards.drink: Fino sherry, aged Rioja or Cava

timeline.what: Open the jamón packs and let them come to room temperature.
Cut the truffle cheese into thin slabs and the Manchego into triangles.
Cut the quince paste into thin squares.
Brush the truffle clean; shave a few slices over the cheese.
Build the board and shave the rest of the truffle at the table.

boards.title: 20 Guests for $60
boards.label: 20 guests for $60
boards.buys: For a crowd, two simple boards beat one fancy one. $60 buys the same cheap, popular foods in party quantities, laid out as two mirror-image boards so guests can eat from both sides.
boards.drink: Punch, beer or sparkling water
boards.board: Two 18 by 12 inch boards, end to end

timeline.what: Cube all the cheese.
Slice both summer sausages into coins.
Fold the salami.
Snip the grapes; fill the ranch bowl.
Build both boards at once, mirror images.

boards.title: 30 Guests for $90
boards.label: 30 guests for $90
boards.buys: At 30 guests, warehouse-club sizes start to pay off: two-pound cheese blocks and pound packs of meat. $90 buys one big board and two side bowls of vegetables and dip.
boards.drink: Lemonade, beer or a big-batch punch
boards.board: One 30 by 18 inch board plus two serving bowls

timeline.what: Cube all three cheeses and mix them together.
Cut the celery into sticks; rinse the broccoli and carrots.
Fold the salami; fan the pepperoni.
Rinse the strawberries and grapes.
Build the board and fill the two side bowls.

boards.title: 50 Guests for $150
boards.label: 50 guests for $150
boards.buys: At 50 guests the board becomes a grazing table: food laid straight onto brown paper, with three boards set into it. $150 covers three meats, three cheeses, two brie wheels, fruit, vegetables and two dips.
boards.drink: Iced tea, lemonade or a beer bucket
boards.board: Grazing spread on kraft paper, about 6 feet

timeline.what: Make the ham pinwheels; wrap and chill. Cube the cheese.
Cover the table with kraft paper; set the three boards.
Cut the pineapple and vegetables.
Slice the pinwheels; fold the salami.
Lay the food in bands and fill every gap.

boards.title: 100 Guests for $300
boards.label: 100 guests for $300
boards.buys: For a graduation or a wedding party, $300 feeds 100 guests at under $3 each when the board sits beside other food. Buy the bulk items at Sam's Club and the small packs at Aldi, where they're cheapest.
boards.drink: Lemonade, iced tea, punch and water
boards.board: 8-foot grazing table on kraft paper, with two crate risers

timeline.what: Make and chill the pinwheels. Cube the cheese. Wash the produce.
Paper the table and set the crate risers.
Cut the pineapple, cucumbers and celery; peel the clementines.
Slice the pinwheels; cut the brie and gouda.
Lay the bands from the far end toward the near end.
